- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., recent sentiment > 0.67 and rising), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp sentiment spike (e.g., sentiment change > 0.50), model often overshoots; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to peak values.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., sentiment < 0.33 or change < -0.33), model overestimates recovery; lower forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above/below recent 7-day average.
- When news volume is constant (as in all examples), model error correlates with sentiment volatility — higher volatility → higher forecast error → apply smoothing filter to reduce noise.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early days of 30-day horizon (e.g., day 1–5) — adjust downward by 2–5% for first 5 days if sentiment is weak or mixed.
